basis: Isolated microphthalmia and coloboma with visual impairment; developmental delay in one assessed patient does not establish common neurologic involvement.
Nonautoimmune thyroid hyperfunction; global developmental delay is frequent (30-79%). Tachycardia and diarrhea alone do not establish heart or gut damage.
Trigeminal nerve dysfunction defines the disease; vascular tortuosity does not establish vascular injury, and feeding difficulty does not establish gut damage.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure (28/29) and dysphagia (23/24) reflect respiratory and bulbar muscle dysfunction rather than intrinsic lung or gut disease.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy, ataxia and other central neurologic manifestations; no common damage outside the nervous system is established.
Hereditary marrow disorder with myelodysplasia, cytopenias and myeloid leukemia; no additional organ involvement is established.
Migraine with motor aura is neurologic; visual, auditory and motor aura symptoms do not establish lasting eye, ear or skeletal muscle damage.
Developmental impairment in 4/4; external ear malformation (microtia) in 4/4; intestinal aganglionosis with megacolon in 2/4 (~50%). Facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy with hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury; hypertension commonly accompanies renal injury.
Glutaminase deficiency causes hyperglutaminemia and a defining neurologic syndrome: developmental delay and progressive cerebellar ataxia in 3/3.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Benign neoplasm originates in the urethra; the renal axis includes the lower urinary tract.
Down syndrome defines a neurodevelopmental disorder; congenital heart defects occur in ~40-50%. Thyroid disease and recurrent ear infections are separate diagnoses.
Leukoplakia confined to vaginal mucosa affects a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency from defective B-cell maturation; recurrent respiratory and ear infections are separate diseases, without established chronic organ damage.
Migraine is a neurologic disorder; vascular terminology does not establish cardiovascular damage, and nausea or light sensitivity does not establish gut or eye injury.
Carcinoma originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes; keratinization does not make it a skin cancer.
Secondary erythrocytosis is a blood-cell disorder; the underlying cause of hypoxia is separate and does not establish pulmonary or cardiovascular involvement.
Umbrella disorder of tyrosine metabolism; hepatic, renal, ocular, skin and neurologic injury vary by subtype and are not established across most of the group.
Carcinoma originates in the extrahepatic bile ducts, included in the hepatic axis.
Intraoral teratoma; direct upper-airway obstruction is a common major manifestation (~30% or more). Intracranial extension is not established as common.
Eye, dental and septal heart defects define OFCD; synostosis and toe contractures are frequent (30-79%). Intellectual disability in 1/3 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Dysferlinopathies cause skeletal muscle degeneration and weakness; neurological ancestry does not establish nerve disease, and heart or lung injury is not typical.
Defining joint contractures, skeletal muscle atrophy and anterior horn cell degeneration; respiratory insufficiency reflects neuromuscular dysfunction; bladder enlargement is absent.
Cerebellar degeneration and motor neuropathy; skeletal muscle atrophy in 6/13 (~46%). Strabismus is a motor manifestation; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness.
